::: {#thm-level-order}
#### Level order goes level by level

In the level order (@def-level-order) of a binary tree that is not empty,
every vertex at level $k$ (@def-tree-level) comes before every vertex at level $k + 1$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $T$ and $r$ be as in @def-level-order.
For each vertex $v$, a walk (@def-walk) from $r$ to $v$ of the smallest length is a path (@thm-walk-path),
and the only path from $r$ to $v$ (@thm-tree-paths) has length $\operatorname{level}(v)$,
so $\operatorname{dist}(r, v) = \operatorname{level}(v)$ (@def-graph-distance).
Since $T$ is connected, @thm-bfs-distance says that `bfs(T, r)` marks every vertex $v$,
with $\texttt{dist}[v] = \operatorname{dist}(r, v) = \operatorname{level}(v)$.
By @lem-bfs-order, the vertices leave the queue with their labels $\texttt{dist}$ in nondecreasing order.
So the levels of the vertices in the level order never decrease,
and every vertex at level $k$ comes before every vertex at level $k + 1$.

:::

:::
